decision: Source-clear for one exact bounded fake-transport test invocation
resolved_findings: The former broad catch could clear an already dispatched replacement fence when a later exact GET failed affirmatively unsent. Current nested classification belongs solely to the initial POST invocation; later read/proof/caller failures retain the fence.
The proven returned snapshot and concurrently replaced latest snapshot each restore only their privately saved actual authority flags.

Per-account exclusive Web Lock check/install/delete is synchronous and uses ifAvailable=true. Busy or unavailable admission fails closed, and a changed persisted attempt cannot be deleted by an older owner.
Lock diagnostic wording no longer implies an earlier POST was unsent. Cross-realm test comparisons normalize actual observations without relaxing compared fields.
reviewed_boundaries: Exact source-derived multipart body is serialized and read once; its actual file slice supplies the digest.
Current signer generation, origin, service, target, session identity, version, ordered complete file facts and caller lifetime are rechecked around awaits and immediately before dispatch.
Persistent uncertainty stores bounded public selectors and metadata only. It blocks mutations and ambiguous discovery across reloaded owners.

Explicit reconciliation uses exact-session GET and compares stable target identity, version, original digest/size/name/MIME, complete neighbours/order/groups and draft hash. No mutation retry is performed.
An unchanged no-op cannot resolve a lost original response; it requires the actual original success response.

Fake suite replaces every service/signer/request/catalogue/decoder/storage/Web Lock primitive. Only the audited adapter, local validation, serializer, Error definitions and Node built-ins execute. Race tests have finite explicit gates and selected 2-second timeouts.
limits: No real browser Web Lock, NIP-98 verification, network, image decoding, database or publication qualification.
An actual browser/strict build remains necessary before claiming UI operation.
The unchanged commit sessionStorage design is outside this replacement-lock claim; no universal cross-tab single-dispatch claim is made.
